title: Wewelsburg Castle seances of Himmler's SS knights

tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Himmler turning Wewelsburg Castle into a ritual center with a round table for his SS knights.

plain: Heinrich Himmler, the head of Hitler's SS, is said to have turned Wewelsburg Castle in Germany into a ritual centre, with a round table where twelve SS "knights" sat and held seances. The author Peter Levenda tells this from his own visit: he went to the castle for a TV segment 10 to 20 years ago. He describes it as a beautiful castle that was falling apart when Himmler took it over and refurbished it "with concentration camp labor," building "basically a round table for his 12 knights to sit around and have seances." Michels tells it separately in his own words, saying Himmler made the castle a ritual centre "complete with a black sun chamber beneath it," a room under the castle named for a symbol, "and a round table for his SS knights." Michels does not mention seances or the forced labour. The story is told because it would show the Nazi leadership mixing state power with occult ritual.
